method: Native original printed banks reread at 4× or 2× inspection. Measured guide observations define a shape-preserving cubic search corridor; original unblurred grayscale cross-sections sampled every 5 native pixels, tangent-averaged over 5 pixels, are jointly matched to ink centres within +/-10 pixels using squared offset-change penalty 3 and squared absolute-offset penalty 0.08. The tiny Gedong wedge uses direct measured bank centres without automatic snapping, preserving its paired banks. Shape-preserving cubic interpolation of these measured ink centres is sampled at at most 1.5 pixels. No image blur, classification dilation, freehand geographic polygon or ground-coordinate adjustment. Source guides and full sampled vectors retained; endpoints remain on source-bank reaches. The acute Murai head also uses directly measured bank centres, preserving a single non-crossing pointed source head. Final physical-bank guides were checked against constrained native cross-sections normal to the coast: only the nearest local dark shore-stroke centre within 6 px was read, never text/grid walking. The guide direction identifies the source bank before interpolation.
limits: G9 prints 1911, edition February 1912, revised February 1916; these local bank corrections do not change source-date substitution.
Source ink is several pixels wide and place-name lettering crosses some banks. Digitisation represents printed ink centres, not a survey measurement.
Ground registration unchanged; 19-control regularised TPS LOO RMS 109.15 m and max 242.08 m remain diagnostics, not a bound on unsampled NW coast accuracy.
Only the visibly printed paired-bank extent is retained at Gedong and Murai; single-line upstream drainage is not widened into mapped water.
witnessMethod: Eight independent wet/dry readings from original raw/G9.jpg, one pair per changed bank arc. Original native scan inspected at 2× overview, 4× headland detail and 6× Gedong/Murai paired-bank mouths. Wet points are within the printed green-water fill; dry points are on beige headland/ground. Points avoid shoreline strokes, the square graticule and printed labels; very narrow paired creeks remain source-generalised. Witnesses were selected from the source image rather than generated vector coordinates. Final additional ten source points cover the five appended arcs; 4× original-source crops were independently inspected, with clear fill points chosen away from bank strokes, text and graticule.
